title: Methanesulfonic Acid as a Dual‐Role Reagent for Porous Polymer Network Design
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The need to develop new materials for energy and environmental sustainability has drawn significant attention in recent years due to population growth, depletion of raw materials, and rising costs. Porous materials are at the center of this quest, necessitating facile approaches for their synthesis, as well as for both pristine and post‐synthetically modified sorbents. This is crucial to reduce chemical waste and hazards involved in the process. Methanesulfonic acid (MSA) is currently being explored as a reagent for the design and fabrication of porous polymer networks (PPNs), with several successful reports so far in the literature. This perspective highlights the overall properties and benefits of MSA for the design of PPNs. A better understanding of MSA's capabilities will open new frontiers and help overcome the limitations of difficult‐to‐scale PPNs. This is because although these PPNs are robust, they still suffer major techno‐economic setbacks that hinder their integration into industrial processes. In addition to the cost of starting materials, which pose a challenge to commercialization, the synthetic approach also contributes significantly. As MSA can play the role of both a solvent and an acid catalyst in a reaction, it is a promising dual‐role reagent for the design of PPNs.

title: Polyacrylate‐Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High‐Performance Artificial Muscles
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate‐based DEFAs (PA‐DEFAs) from a bimodal‐networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s
                    −1
                    . The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core‐to‐shell flow‐rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch‐free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg
                    −
                    1
                    , and a peak power density of 443 W kg
                    −
                    1
                    —outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel‐connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta‐ray with modular fault‐tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA‐DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing‐compatible platform for next‐generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.

title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel,
                    2
                    , shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC
                    50
                     = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H
                    +
                    /Cl
                    −
                     = 249.7; H
                    +
                    /Na
                    +
                     = 23.9; H
                    +
                    /K
                    +
                     = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment,
                    2
                    mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly,
                    2
                    exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC
                    50
                    < 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel‐mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

title: Negative‐Thermal‐Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium‐ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na
                    +
                    intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore‐filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW
                    2
                    O
                    8
                    . The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high‐rate and long‐term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (−20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.

title: Self‐Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme‐rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano‐engineered
                    Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
                    (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist‐loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor‐associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer‐associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK‐cell‐associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain‐related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.

title: Tuning N‐Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni1Aun‐SrTiO3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Inefficient generation of N‐related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N
                    2
                    , has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N
                    2
                    , CO
                    2
                    , and H
                    2
                    O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N‐related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni
                    1
                    Au
                    n
                    active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu‐STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N
                    2
                    adsorption/activation and effective generation of N‐related intermediates to facilitate C–N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg g
                    cat.
                    −1
                    , with successful crystallization of a collectible solid‐phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction‐temperature programmed desorption‐mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N
                    2
                    , which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N
                    2
                    and confirm the formation of critical N‐related intermediates (e.g., *NH
                    2
                    ) on the NiAu‐STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C–N coupling intermediate (*NH
                    2
                    COO
                    –
                    ) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N
                    2
                    , CO
                    2
                    , and H
                    2
                    O.

title: High‐Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape‐memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s
                    −1
                    , and a peak power density of 6105 W kg
                    −1
                    . Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10‐fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing‐flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.

title: High‐Entropy Ceramic‐Enhanced Deformable Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Noncontact Biomechanical and Raindrop Energy Harvesting (Adv. Mater. 58/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Noncontact Biomechanical and Raindrop Energy Harvesting In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74157), Heng-Jui Liu, Cheolmin Park, Ying-Chih Lai, and co-workers report a large-area, fully deformable high-entropy ceramic particle-doped triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG). The high-entropy effect arising from multielement incorporation substantially enhances the triboelectric charge-trapping capability, while the carbonized fabric interlayer serves as a reservoir for storing triboelectric charges. The TENG demonstrates broad practical applicability, including contact/non-contact human biomechanical energy harvesting and large-area distributed raindrop energy harvesting.

title: Single‐Photon Superradiance in Giant Rhombicuboctahedral CsPbI3 Nanocrystals (Adv. Mater. 58/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Single-Photon Superradiance The cover image illustrates a giant rhombicuboctahedral CsPbI3 nanocrystal exhibiting single-photon superradiance. By employing a novel phenacyl iodide precursor, these weakly confined large nanocrystals maintain an exceptional high photoluminescence quantum yield. At cryogenic temperatures, coherent dipole coupling induces a giant oscillator strength; this quantum effect allows the nanocrystals to emit ultrafast, high-purity superradiance single photons. More details can be found in the Research Article by Ping-Hsun Tsai, Ken-Tsung Wong, Hao-Wu Lin, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74549).

title: Sustainable Poly(Lactic Acid)/Graphene Oxide Bioelectronic Platform for Neurotransmitters Sensing and Tunable Stimulation of Astrocytes (Adv. Mater. 58/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Sustainable Laser-Scribed Bioelectronics In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74487), Valentina Benfenati, Chiara Zanardi, Emanuele Treossi, and co-workers report biocompatible and biodegradable laser-scribed graphene-like electrodes with tunable electrical and physicochemical properties. By controlling laser fluence, conductive traces with tailored resistance and electrocatalytic activity enable sensitive neurotrasnmitters detection and antifouling performance. The same platform enables tunable and selective electrical stimulation of Ca2+ signaling in primary astrocytes. Overall, the authors reported a sustainable strategy for bidirectional bioelectronic communication with neural cells.

title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η6–Arene Catalyst
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function (
                    η
                    6
                    –arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables
                    contra
                    ‐thermodynamic
                    E
                    ‐to‐
                    Z
                    isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar (
                    E
                    )‐stilbenes over twisted (
                    Z
                    )‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi1–Bi2 Sites
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO
                    2
                    reduction toward multi‐carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic‐kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft‐confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi
                    1
                    –Bi
                    2
                    coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen‐bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO
                    2
                    coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi
                    1
                    –Bi
                    2
                    sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft‐hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br to achieve a CH
                    3
                    COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent‐free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation–Anion Co‐Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multivalent cation–anion co‐(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge‐compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre‐intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation mechanism—organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg
                    2
                    +
                    ‐TFSI
                    −
                    as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm
                    −
                    2
                    and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm
                    −
                    2
                    , surpassing leading Mg‐ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co‐(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high‐performance energy storage.
